purpose: Concrete next research questions; queued items are not completed work or product recommendations.

items.question: Distinguish one-user, one-device and site-wide faults with a repeatable intake exercise
items.deliverable: Create three sanitized intake examples that arrive at different correct guides.
items.acceptance: Each example includes the actual discriminator, private-evidence boundary and measurable acceptance.

items.question: Reduce repeat visits caused by missing baseline evidence
items.deliverable: Compare a minimal intake record against recurring repair handoff gaps.
items.acceptance: A second technician can resume each example without asking for the original symptom again.

items.question: Validate the cleanup route on supported ARM and managed endpoints
items.deliverable: Document the supported alternative when offline scanning is unavailable.
items.acceptance: Primary platform support, management constraints and post-cleanup acceptance are explicit.

items.question: Distinguish browser notification abuse from endpoint compromise
items.deliverable: Add a reproducible browser-permission and extension investigation using clean examples.
items.acceptance: The guide separates site permissions, account compromise and host persistence without overclaiming a clean scan.

items.question: Rehearse identity containment after endpoint isolation
items.deliverable: Write a tabletop sequence for token/session revocation and recovery-account access.
items.acceptance: The sequence preserves evidence and defines who can authorize tenant-wide actions.

items.question: Prove a clean recovery boundary before reconnecting restored machines
items.deliverable: Create a restore-and-rejoin tabletop with separated backup and identity checks.
items.acceptance: Recovery evidence includes backup provenance, identity control and a monitored acceptance task.

items.question: Compare bottlenecks using equivalent workloads
items.deliverable: Capture CPU, memory, storage and thermal observations for the same reproducible task.
items.acceptance: Recommendations follow the observed limiting resource; before/after conditions are equivalent.

items.question: Evaluate startup and background-service changes reversibly
items.deliverable: Document one narrowly scoped startup change with rollback and a measured original task.
items.acceptance: No blanket service disabling; the evidence shows benefit or an explicit revert.

items.question: Compare repair paths when Windows still boots
items.deliverable: Compare component repair, same-version repair reinstall and applicable restore options.
items.acceptance: A decision table covers preserved data, prerequisites, policy restrictions and post-repair tests.

items.question: Handle an unavailable repair source without random image substitution
items.deliverable: Document supported source matching and servicing evidence collection.
items.acceptance: Version, language and architecture constraints are sourced and errors route to a concrete next step.

items.question: Diagnose feature-update rollback from preserved setup logs
items.deliverable: Work through a sanitized setup failure and the exact log evidence needed.
items.acceptance: The diagnosis identifies an actionable compatibility or setup finding and a supported remedy.

items.question: Separate managed update policy from a damaged update client
items.deliverable: Add an organization-managed endpoint decision branch.
items.acceptance: The guide identifies the policy owner and avoids undoing deliberate deferral or deployment controls.

items.question: Exercise recovery options on UEFI and encrypted systems
items.deliverable: Run a documented lab recovery with recovery-key access and unambiguous target volumes.
items.acceptance: Both boot identity and file access are verified; commands never assume recovery drive letters.

items.question: Evaluate connected recovery on a supported outage scenario
items.deliverable: Compare the current connected recovery capability with ordinary local recovery.
items.acceptance: Supported builds, network prerequisites and an exit route are documented without universal claims.

items.question: Validate imaging stop conditions with readable error evidence
items.deliverable: Prepare a disposable-media lab for mapfile continuation and destination verification.
items.acceptance: Source/destination identities, retry policy and evidence-preservation boundaries are recorded.

items.question: Distinguish deleted data from lost encryption access
items.deliverable: Build a decision branch for deleted files, missing volumes and unavailable recovery keys.
items.acceptance: The guide explains what recovery tooling can and cannot restore in each branch.

items.question: Test cloning across different logical sector sizes
items.deliverable: Research supported migration constraints and prove a compatible disposable-disk workflow.
items.acceptance: The guide states capacity, sector and boot constraints with an actual boot and file acceptance.

items.question: Verify encryption and recovery after SSD migration
items.deliverable: Document the post-migration encryption, recovery and backup checks.
items.acceptance: The original remains recoverable until the new disk passes boot, workload and recovery checks.

items.question: Restore a representative app data set on an isolated target
items.deliverable: Define a realistic restore exercise for files plus application metadata.
items.acceptance: Restore time, permissions and application-level acceptance are recorded separately from backup completion.

items.question: Test disconnected or immutable recovery copies
items.deliverable: Compare available copy-protection approaches for a small office.
items.acceptance: Threat model, restoration access and ongoing cost are explicit; marketing claims are not accepted as proof.

items.question: Distinguish IPv6 path failures from DNS faults
items.deliverable: Create a controlled dual-stack diagnosis with explicit IPv4 and IPv6 comparisons.
items.acceptance: The evidence isolates the failing path without globally disabling a supported protocol.

items.question: Diagnose Wi-Fi roaming and intermittent loss
items.deliverable: Collect reproducible link, latency and signal observations while moving between access points.
items.acceptance: The guide separates RF coverage, authentication, DHCP and upstream connectivity with privacy-safe evidence.

items.question: Rehearse a staged small-office power restoration
items.deliverable: Create a dependency-aware restoration exercise for power, network, identity and workloads.
items.acceptance: Acceptance follows dependencies and records failed-device stop conditions.

items.question: Verify UPS event evidence and safe shutdown behavior
items.deliverable: Review current supported monitoring routes for the actual deployed UPS family.
items.acceptance: A controlled test validates alerting and shutdown without claiming a paper configuration works.

items.question: Compare attended support routes under restrictive policies
items.deliverable: Test supported consent, elevation, reconnect and session-end behavior.
items.acceptance: Business licensing, network requirements and positive session termination are verified.

items.question: Verify accessible remote-help instructions with a novice user
items.deliverable: Walk through the exact join and end-session path using simple labels.
items.acceptance: A user can reach support and revoke access without sharing a password or guessing the right button.

items.question: Differentiate trust failure from clock and DNS problems
items.deliverable: Build a domain-member lab case that fails for each separate cause.
items.acceptance: Each branch tests the cause before repair and verifies the intended identity context.

items.question: Document a managed local-admin recovery path
items.deliverable: Review the approved password-recovery and rotation workflow for the managed environment.
items.acceptance: Only authorized access is described, and the guide distinguishes identity recovery from domain trust repair.

items.question: Compare current Outlook clients for repair prerequisites
items.deliverable: Verify feature, profile, add-in and offline-data differences for supported clients.
items.acceptance: Guidance names the client and account type instead of applying a classic-client procedure universally.

items.question: Prove whether mail failure is delivery, sync or local display
items.deliverable: Build a sender-to-mailbox-to-client diagnostic example.
items.acceptance: Message timestamps and server evidence identify the failing layer without deleting the only local copy.

items.question: Verify protected-print and vendor-driver workflows by capability
items.deliverable: Test printing and scanning requirements on representative compatible devices.
items.acceptance: Model, OS, policy, duplex, tray and scanning requirements determine the supported route.

items.question: Reproduce queue failures after DHCP address changes
items.deliverable: Test reserved addressing and queue-port alignment in a small lab.
items.acceptance: The printer identity is verified, the target queue is changed alone and a real document prints.

items.question: Separate driver crashes from unstable hardware in a repeatable lab
items.deliverable: Compare dump evidence, temperature and one-variable hardware checks.
items.acceptance: The guide distinguishes evidence from correlation and avoids unsupervised stress on failing equipment.

items.question: Interpret battery health and charging limits accurately
items.deliverable: Review supported battery reports and manufacturer diagnostics.
items.acceptance: Capacity, workload, charge limit and actual runtime are separated; no universal percentage threshold is invented.

items.question: Validate a repeatable workstation acceptance checklist
items.deliverable: Rebuild a disposable workstation with current supported setup and package routes.
items.acceptance: Identity, encryption recovery, updates, backup, printers and the real user workload all pass.

items.question: Prove profile and cloud-file migration completeness
items.deliverable: Compare local folders, cloud-only placeholders and app-specific data before cutover.
items.acceptance: Counts alone do not establish completeness; representative files and app behavior are checked.

items.question: Test whether a second technician can resume the case
items.deliverable: Use sanitized interrupted cases to assess continuation records.
items.acceptance: Each record includes the last change, result, rollback, remaining risk and exact next action.

items.question: Create a plain-language customer acceptance exercise
items.deliverable: Test handoff wording for repairs, remaining limitations and follow-up dates.
items.acceptance: The original task is demonstrated and the client can explain the agreed next step.

items.question: Validate rescue media with Secure Boot and current firmware
items.deliverable: Test BIOS/UEFI and supported Secure Boot paths using verified images.
items.acceptance: Media identity, boot evidence, hardware limits and reversion to the normal boot order are recorded.

items.question: Verify offline access to the complete technician kit
items.deliverable: Build an offline drill for drivers, recovery keys, documentation and essential utilities.
items.acceptance: Everything claimed to work offline is exercised; account and network dependencies are labeled.

items.question: Compare AI diagnosis quality on sanitized known-outcome cases
items.deliverable: Create a fixed evaluation set and score diagnoses, unsupported claims and useful next tests.
items.acceptance: No live customer data is used and improvement is measured against a baseline.

items.question: Validate local model resource and data-handling boundaries
items.deliverable: Measure a permitted local workflow on the actual target hardware.
items.acceptance: Memory, latency, network behavior and cleanup are documented separately from answer quality.

items.question: Use failure trends to prioritize maintenance tasks
items.deliverable: Compare a quarter of sanitized recurring symptoms against planned work.
items.acceptance: Tasks reduce observed risk and have acceptance evidence rather than ceremonial cleanup.

items.question: Validate the recovery plan after a scheduled maintenance change
items.deliverable: Exercise backup restoration and selected workload checks after a reversible update.
items.acceptance: The change is accepted only after the real task and rollback/recovery path are checked.

items.question: Recheck supported-platform and business-use limits for the cleanup kit
items.deliverable: A comparison of supported architectures, managed-endpoint constraints and scanner roles.
items.acceptance: Compare against the current catalog, record adopt/retain/evaluate decisions and do not claim runtime proof from documentation.

items.question: Compare current recovery, cloning, sync and backup roles
items.deliverable: A decision table that prevents using sync as backup or repair as recovery.
items.acceptance: Compare against the current catalog, record adopt/retain/evaluate decisions and do not claim runtime proof from documentation.

items.question: Compare current Windows repair and diagnostic capabilities
items.deliverable: Supported-build and policy-aware choices with exact launch/acquisition paths.
items.acceptance: Compare against the current catalog, record adopt/retain/evaluate decisions and do not claim runtime proof from documentation.

items.question: Compare attended support setup burden and session termination
items.deliverable: A consent-to-disconnect comparison with licensing and elevation behavior.
items.acceptance: Compare against the current catalog, record adopt/retain/evaluate decisions and do not claim runtime proof from documentation.

items.question: Compare manufacturer diagnostics with specialist observation tools
items.deliverable: A model-aware selection guide covering logs, thermal readings and test limits.
items.acceptance: Compare against the current catalog, record adopt/retain/evaluate decisions and do not claim runtime proof from documentation.

items.question: Compare discovery, packet capture and path-diagnostic setup burden
items.deliverable: Evidence-based quick choices with platform, permissions and output interpretation.
items.acceptance: Compare against the current catalog, record adopt/retain/evaluate decisions and do not claim runtime proof from documentation.

items.question: Compare maintained rescue-media and network-boot paths
items.deliverable: Verified source identity and supported firmware/architecture/dependency notes.
items.acceptance: Compare against the current catalog, record adopt/retain/evaluate decisions and do not claim runtime proof from documentation.

items.question: Compare useful technician utilities against already-covered capabilities
items.deliverable: Additions only for a named service gap, with official acquisition and business-use evidence.
items.acceptance: Compare against the current catalog, record adopt/retain/evaluate decisions and do not claim runtime proof from documentation.

items.question: Compare current defensive telemetry and managed identity tools
items.deliverable: Deployment prerequisites, scope, data retention and reversible investigation routes.
items.acceptance: Compare against the current catalog, record adopt/retain/evaluate decisions and do not claim runtime proof from documentation.

items.question: Evaluate AI troubleshooting tools against a fixed sanitized case set
items.deliverable: Measured answer usefulness, data handling, hardware requirements and failure cases.
items.acceptance: Compare against the current catalog, record adopt/retain/evaluate decisions and do not claim runtime proof from documentation.

items.question: Validate printer discovery across trusted and isolated Wi-Fi
items.deliverable: Exercise the new isolation and blocked-queue branches on a representative printer with a sanitized topology and actual output.
items.acceptance: Discovery, printing and scanning results are recorded independently; guest isolation remains intentional and the affected queue is identified.

items.question: Exercise the client-specific auth, search and storage branches
items.deliverable: Run disposable-account tests for Google authorization, a known search result and an Outlook.com quota error.
items.acceptance: Record account type, client build, two-way delivery and content preservation; documentation review is not labeled a live test.

items.question: Prove recovery of a failed VSS writer through a real restore
items.deliverable: Use a disposable workload to record the failed writer, targeted recovery, completed backup and restored application data.
items.acceptance: The writer owner and service interruption are explicit; a successful backup status is followed by a usable restored workload.

items.question: Recheck service ownership, free/account boundaries, submission visibility and actual launch destinations after provider changes.
items.deliverable: A dated review of changed official plans, moved applications and useful new online services without duplicate product entries.
items.acceptance: Every accepted change has primary evidence and consistent app, Wiki and first-action routes; inaccessible or retired candidates remain explicitly recorded.
